note: Vocabulary Description Length is a single-hook module: hook_form_taxonomy_vocabulary_form_alter sets the Description element's #type to 'textarea' so long descriptions are practical to type. It has NO config, schema, permissions, services, Drush or configure route, and does NOT change storage - a vocabulary description is an unlimited string in taxonomy.vocabulary.<vid> either way. Because its only effect is on the vocabulary form widget (observable only by rendering that admin form), the medium/hard cases are grounded in the vocabulary config the module targets: introspection reads a vocabulary's (long) description; execution builds a vocabulary that HAS a long multi-line description (the end state the module enables). Fixtures are created with raw config writes because full config-entity saves via the entity API are currently blocked by an unrelated broken commerce_giftcard field on this shared site.

evals.prompt: What does the Drupal module vocabulary_description_length change, and how? Which form does it alter and what does it do to the description field?
evals.expected_output: It implements hook_form_FORM_ID_alter() for taxonomy_vocabulary_form and sets the Description element's #type to 'textarea' (instead of core's single-line textfield), so editors can comfortably enter long, multi-line vocabulary descriptions.

evals.prompt: If I install vocabulary_description_length, does it change how or where a vocabulary's description is stored, or add a length limit? Does it need any configuration?
evals.expected_output: No. It has no configuration and no configure route. It only changes the vocabulary form widget (textfield -> textarea); the description is still stored as an unlimited string in the taxonomy.vocabulary.<vid> config object, with no new length limit or validation and no front-end change.

evals.prompt: Does vocabulary_description_length affect taxonomy term descriptions or other entity forms, or only the vocabulary form?
evals.expected_output: Only the vocabulary form (taxonomy_vocabulary_form). It does not touch term descriptions or any other form/entity - its single form-alter is scoped to the vocabulary add/edit form.

evals.prompt: One taxonomy vocabulary on this site has a long, multi-paragraph description. Inspect the live configuration, name that vocabulary (its machine name), and summarise what its description is about.
evals.expected_output: The vocabulary vdl_known has a long description (about editorial tag governance/naming conventions and term review). Read it with `drush cget taxonomy.vocabulary.vdl_known description`.

evals.prompt: This site has two vocabularies, vdl_long and vdl_short. Inspect their live configuration and state which one has the long multi-paragraph description.
evals.expected_output: vdl_long has the long description; vdl_short has only a short one-line description. Compare `drush cget taxonomy.vocabulary.vdl_long description` and `... vdl_short description`.

evals.prompt: On this Drupal site (which has vocabulary_description_length enabled so long descriptions are supported), create a taxonomy vocabulary with machine name vdl_task and give it a long, multi-paragraph description (several sentences across more than one line explaining its purpose and editorial rules). Apply it to the live site.
evals.expected_output: Create taxonomy vocabulary vdl_task whose description is a multi-line string of at least ~200 characters (the vocabulary form's textarea, provided by this module, makes such a description practical to enter).

evals.prompt: The vocabulary vdl_edit on this site currently has only a short one-line description. Replace it with a long, multi-paragraph description (several sentences across multiple lines) documenting the vocabulary's purpose and usage rules. Apply the change to the live site.
evals.expected_output: Update taxonomy vocabulary vdl_edit so its description is a multi-line string of at least ~200 characters.
